passage.quote:
A separate binary64 PTX backend runs the repeated matrix-free operator and
conjugate-gradient arithmetic on the GPU, using the Lean reference for mesh,
quadrature, load and diagonal setup. Its empirical comparison, memory checks
and execution evidence are distinct from a formal PTX correspondence theorem.

summary: Run the matrix-free Poisson operator and PCG iterations in binary64 PTX using mesh, quadrature, load and diagonal setup supplied by Lean.
Use disjoint element storage and one writer per global node for deterministic ordered assembly without floating-point atomics.
Certify accepted solutions with an exact residual checker for the represented coefficients; retain separate instruction-correspondence obligations.
Prove whole-cell tensor correspondence from actual gathering, all eight contractions, barrier visibility and publication of computed stores.
Prove complete assembly entry correctness and general returning execution from valid arrays, including boundary masking and inactive-thread return.
Derive assembly read visibility from one joint history and prove its published ordered scatter; construct admitted returning parallel witnesses for arbitrary valid inputs.
Connect the complete true_residual kernel to its subtraction specification under explicit byte-source constraints.
Check emitted entries and launch shapes against Lean representations, preserving numerical order and the distinction between proof checking and GPU observations.
Compose actual cell publications with assembly using checked ordered input tables, preserving uploaded metadata and the TorchLean operator result.
Connect unmasked PTX cell/assembly publication directly to the public array-based TorchLean reference, preserving its validation and rounded scatter order.

Keep arbitrary-input whole-cell existence, serialized setup representation, remaining PCG/reduction instructions, launch composition, complete PTX admission and hardware conformance as separate obligations.
Interleave actual cell instructions across blocks, derive local source admission, and connect chronological store publication through assembly to the reference operator.
Construct an admitted grid schedule from supplied local cell executions with common entry arguments, without an assumed grid run or result.
Connect cell and assembly stores to fresh-residual subtraction, deriving input preservation and retaining the separate exact-real norm and stopping obligations.
Provide explicit necessary repeated-write visibility rules for in-place reductions, without claiming their full instruction correspondence.
Prove and bind the local rounded tree update while keeping full parallel reduction and solver correspondence explicit remaining work.

from.quote:
One group of GPU threads handles each square element. Successive contractions
apply the one-dimensional basis tables, with barriers separating shared-memory
intermediates. Products and sums use separate explicitly rounded binary64
instructions. Contributions are first written into disjoint element storage.
Every group thread reaches each barrier, including inactive matrix lanes.
A second kernel gives each global node one writer, which sums its incident
contributions in element order. This preserves a deterministic assembly order
without concurrent floating-point updates. Interior solves explicitly zero the
boundary entries; the unrestricted operator is also available for comparison.

passage.quote:
def element(self,name,source):
        m=self.l.m
        body=f'setp.lt.u32 %live, %lane, {m*m};\ndiv.u32 %i, %lane, {m};\nrem.u32 %j, %lane, {m};\n'
        stages=[]
        stages.append(f'mad.lo.u32 %idx, %cell, {m*m}, %lane;\n'+self.load('cells','%node','%idx')+self.load(source,'%value','%node')+self.shared_store(0,'%value'))
        stages.append(self.dot(('B','%i','k'),(0,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(1,'%acc')+
                      self.dot(('D','%i','k'),(0,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(2,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot((1,'%i','k'),('D','%j','k'))+self.load('W','%c','%lane')+
                      'mul.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %c;\n'+self.shared_store(3,'%acc')+
                      self.dot((2,'%i','k'),('B','%j','k'))+self.load('W','%c','%lane')+
                      'mul.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %c;\n'+self.shared_store(4,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot(('B','k','%i'),(3,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(5,'%acc')+
                      self.dot(('D','k','%i'),(4,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(6,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot((5,'%i','k'),('D','k','%j'))+self.dot((6,'%i','k'),('B','k','%j'),'%acc2')+
                      f'add.rn.f64 %value, %acc, %acc2;\nmad.lo.u32 %idx, %cell, {m*m}, %lane;\n'+self.store('element','%value','%idx'))
        for i,stage in enumerate(stages):
            body+=f'@!%live bra stage_{i}_done;\n'+stage+f'stage_{i}_done:\n'
            if i<len(stages)-1:body+='bar.sync 0;\n'
        return self.entry(name,body,32,self.l.n**2,7*m*m*8)
    def assemble(self,name,target,mask):
        body=self.vector_start()+self.load('offsets','%cursor','%global')+'add.u32 %idx, %global, 1;\n'+self.load('offsets','%end','%idx')
        body+=f'mov.f64 %acc, {ZERO};\nloop:\nsetp.ge.u32 %p0, %cursor, %end;\n@%p0 bra done;\n'
        body+=self.load('entries','%idx','%cursor')+self.load('element','%a','%idx')+'add.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %a;\nadd.u32 %cursor, %cursor, 1;\nbra loop;\ndone:\n'
        if mask:body+=self.load('boundary','%flag','%global')+f'setp.ne.u32 %p0, %flag, 0;\n@%p0 mov.f64 %acc, {ZERO};\n'
        return self.entry(name,body+self.store(target,'%acc','%global'))

from.quote:
Vector updates, division by the Jacobi diagonal, dot products and square roots
are implemented in PTX. Dot products use a specified parallel reduction tree.
Their order can differ from the CPU reference, so numerical agreement is tested
rather than assumed bitwise. The loop retains active and broken state, freezes
updates after recursive convergence, recomputes the true residual at scheduled
checks and at the iteration limit, and restarts if the recursive test was too
optimistic. Empty interiors, zero loads, breakdown and exhausted iterations have
explicit outcomes. The recorded suite does not exercise a restart; implementation
of that branch does not imply observed coverage.

Generation validates the uniform connectivity, finite setup arrays, positive
interior diagonal, solver controls and a bounded 32-bit index domain. Device
storage contains guard bytes around every buffer; inputs and guards are checked
after solving. These checks and sanitizer runs support the tested executions,
not a universal memory-safety theorem.

Validation covers Q1–Q4, numerical operator comparisons on supplied and varied
vectors, complete solves, polynomial reproduction, boundary preservation,
iteration limits and invalid inputs. CPU references and device results start
from identical setup arrays. Saved cases, PTX and binary hashes, launch records,
outputs, toolchain identity and sanitizer logs make the observations reproducible.
All failures remain visible; tolerances are declared before running comparisons.
No throughput or benchmarking claim is part of this backend.

The numerical comparison uses fixed absolute and relative tolerances. Rounded
GPU and Lean residual measurements remain diagnostic comparisons and allow a
small measurement discrepancy. Acceptance additionally requires the proved
exact Lean residual checker: the saved setup coefficients and returned solution
must satisfy the requested bound with no extra allowance and exactly zero
boundary values. Iteration-limit and breakdown results are not certified.

            residual_request=dict(case,values=observed['solution'],maxiter=0)
            save(folder/'residual-request.json',[residual_request])
            run([INTEGRATION/'.lake/build/bin/poissonQuad','--request',folder/'residual-request.json','--output',folder/'residual-reference.json'])
            independent=json.loads((folder/'residual-reference.json').read_text())[0]
            if 'error' in independent:raise ValueError(independent['error'])
            residual=math.hypot(*(a-b for a,b,bd in zip(ref['load'],independent['applied'],ref['boundary'],strict=True) if not bd))
            if math.isfinite(residual)!=math.isfinite(observed['true_residual_norm']) or (math.isfinite(residual) and abs(residual-observed['true_residual_norm'])>2e-12+2e-10*residual):
                raise AssertionError('reported residual disagrees with independently applied Lean operator')
            if observed['converged'] and residual>observed['tolerance']+2e-12:
                raise AssertionError('independent residual does not corroborate convergence')

from.quote:
For assembly, every recorded store has its owner's node address, independently
of proposed read values. Input arrays occupy byte ranges disjoint from the
output vector; either physical order is allowed. The actual offset-load
addresses therefore force their bytes to initialization. The resulting cursor
bounds constrain each contribution-index load, whose admitted bytes in turn
bound the cell-value address. This dependency order derives every read footprint
from the same joint history and discharges the replay separation condition.
No desired cursor range, read value or local snapshot execution is assumed.

theorem Arena.read_footprints
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) a.offsets a.entries a.element mask a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start memory (regs i)) words indices t)
    (compatible : IndexSources.Compatible memory words indices indexSource)
    (contents : a.Contents memory) (separated : a.InputSeparation) (thread : Fin n) :
    (∀ read∈Flow.Parallel.wordsFor thread words, read.data.store=false →
      read.space=.global ∧ a.InputRead 8 read.data.address) ∧
    (∀ read∈Flow.Parallel.indicesFor thread indices, a.InputRead 4 read.address) := by

from.quote:
The chronological global stores of that actual interleaving publish the ordered
rounded row sum at each node, with the emitted optional boundary mask. A local
byte changes exactly when its instruction records a global store; other threads
write disjoint node slots. Thus the joint publication agrees with the final
local output word, without assumed store coverage or a supplied publication
schedule. This is mathematical publication of recorded writes, not a CUDA
host-visibility claim.

theorem Arena.parallel_value
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) a.offsets a.entries a.element mask a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start memory (regs i)) words indices t)
    (compatible : Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible (fun space => match space with | .global => memory | .shared => fun _ => 0) words wordSource)
    (indexCompatible : IndexSources.Compatible memory words indices indexSource)
    (contents : a.Contents memory) (separated : a.InputSeparation)
    (done : ∀ i, (t i).halted=true) (thread : Fin n) :
    decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish memory words) (Snapshot.address a thread))=
      a.value memory thread mask := by

from.quote:
Every valid physical assembly input also has a returning joint execution with
compatible initialization sources. Each scalar execution reads its inputs
before its sole output store. Its recorded reads therefore use initial bytes;
combining the returning threads constructs an actual admitted interleaving.
This general existence proof does not depend on interpreter fuel or specific
numerical values. Kernel-checked two-node examples instantiate it with nonzero
values, both masking choices, and a nonzero arena base.

passage.quote:
theorem Arena.parallel_exists_correct (a : Arena n) (memory : Memory) (regs : Fin n → Registers)
    (contents : a.Contents memory) (separated : a.InputSeparation) (mask : Bool) :
    ∃ words indices final,
      Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
        (entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) a.offsets a.entries a.element mask a.boundary a.output)
        (fun i => a.start memory (regs i)) words indices final ∧
      (∀ i, (final i).halted=true) ∧
      Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible (fun space => match space with | .global => memory | .shared => fun _ => 0)
        words (fun _ _ => .initial) ∧
      IndexSources.Compatible memory words indices (fun _ _ => .initial) ∧
      ∀ i, decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish memory words) (Snapshot.address a i))=a.value memory i mask := by

from.quote:
The cell-to-assembly theorem uses the operator's actual connectivity arrays.
A finite checker decodes ordered contribution rows from the uploaded integer
tables. Actual cell executions share one initial global memory; their stores
are confined to their own active output coordinates and preserve assembly
metadata. Publishing these histories and executing assembly produces the
TorchLean tensor operator with the same rounded addition order and optional
boundary mask. A nonzero complete-cell and assembly example checks the
connection without supplying expected intermediate values.

passage.quote:
theorem cell_assembly_operator {o : Operator} {values : Array Float}
    {words : List (Concurrent.Event o.mesh.points.size)}
    {indices : List (Fin o.mesh.points.size × IndexSources.Access)}
    {final : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Flow.State}
    (family : CellWhole.Family o values) (shape : OperatorMesh o)
    (same : o.q.size=o.nodes.size)
    (order : List (Fin o.mesh.cells.size)) (complete : ∀ i, i∈order)
    (a : Assembly.Arena o.mesh.points.size)
    (base : a.base=family.base) (element : a.element=family.output)
    (offsetsBefore : a.offsets.toNat+(o.mesh.points.size+1)*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (entriesBefore : a.entries.toNat+a.entryCount*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (boundaryBefore : a.boundary.toNat+o.mesh.points.size*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (tables : a.RowsEncoded family.memory (Assembly.nodeRows o.mesh.points.size (Assembly.MeshRows.locations shape.connectivity)))
    (separated : a.InputSeparation)
    (regs : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Registers)
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (Assembly.entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 o.mesh.points.size) a.offsets a.entries a.element mask a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start (family.publish family.memory order) (regs i)) words indices final)
    (compatible : Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible
      (fun space => match space with | .global => family.publish family.memory order | .shared => fun _ => 0) words wordSource)
    (indexCompatible : IndexSources.Compatible (family.publish family.memory order) words indices indexSource)
    (done : ∀ i, (final i).halted=true) (node : Fin o.mesh.points.size) :
    decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish (family.publish family.memory order) words) (Assembly.Snapshot.address a node))=
      if mask=true ∧ read32 family.memory (a.base.toNat+a.boundary.toNat+node.val*4)≠0 then 0 else
        shape.operator same values node := by
  rw [← family.input_word32 family.memory order (a.base.toNat+a.boundary.toNat+node.val*4)
    (by rw [base]; have := node.isLt; omega)]
  apply a.parallel_operator shape.connectivity
    (CoefficientRepresentation.rows same o.b) (CoefficientRepresentation.rows same o.d)
    (CoefficientRepresentation.square same o.w) (OperatorMesh.input values)
    run compatible indexCompatible (family.assembly_tables family.memory order a base offsetsBefore entriesBefore tables)
    separated done
  intro cell i j
  rw [CoefficientRepresentation.local_action,← shape.gather]
  have result := family.published_entry family.memory order cell (complete cell) i j
  unfold Assembly.Arena.elementValue
  rw [base,element]
  simpa only [CellWhole.Family.address,Nat.add_mul,Nat.add_assoc,Nat.add_left_comm,Nat.add_comm] using result

from.quote:
The executable array reference and the tensor operator now have a proved
connection. The actual reference loops enumerate cells and local coordinates
in the same order and perform the same rounded updates. With valid finite input,
the public Poisson.apply function returns exactly the vector published by the
unmasked cell/assembly composition; no change to the reference computation or
its input validation is needed.

passage.quote:
theorem cell_assembly_reference {o : Operator} {values : Array Float}
    {words : List (Concurrent.Event o.mesh.points.size)}
    {indices : List (Fin o.mesh.points.size × IndexSources.Access)}
    {final : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Flow.State}
    (family : CellWhole.Family o values) (shape : OperatorMesh o)
    (same : o.q.size=o.nodes.size)
    (order : List (Fin o.mesh.cells.size)) (complete : ∀ i, i∈order)
    (a : Assembly.Arena o.mesh.points.size)
    (base : a.base=family.base) (element : a.element=family.output)
    (offsetsBefore : a.offsets.toNat+(o.mesh.points.size+1)*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (entriesBefore : a.entries.toNat+a.entryCount*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (boundaryBefore : a.boundary.toNat+o.mesh.points.size*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (tables : a.RowsEncoded family.memory (Assembly.nodeRows o.mesh.points.size (Assembly.MeshRows.locations shape.connectivity)))
    (separated : a.InputSeparation)
    (regs : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Registers)
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (Assembly.entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 o.mesh.points.size) a.offsets a.entries a.element false a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start (family.publish family.memory order) (regs i)) words indices final)
    (compatible : Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible
      (fun space => match space with | .global => family.publish family.memory order | .shared => fun _ => 0) words wordSource)
    (indexCompatible : IndexSources.Compatible (family.publish family.memory order) words indices indexSource)
    (done : ∀ i, (final i).halted=true)
    (size : values.size=o.mesh.points.size) (finite : values.all Float.isFinite=true) :
    Poisson.apply o values=.ok (Array.ofFn fun node : Fin o.mesh.points.size =>
      decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish (family.publish family.memory order) words)
        (Assembly.Snapshot.address a node))) := by
  rw [ArrayOperator.apply_correspondence o shape same values size finite]
  congr 1
  apply congrArg Array.ofFn
  funext node
  have result := cell_assembly_operator family shape same order complete a base element
    offsetsBefore entriesBefore boundaryBefore tables separated regs run compatible indexCompatible done node
  simpa only [Bool.false_eq_true,false_and,ite_false] using result.symm
